clue.text: Spin doctor uses power move in the gym?

parts.note: a spin doctor works in public relations, abbreviated PR

indicators.note: to move things is to shift them about, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor exerts influence, which the question mark recasts as working out at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' does double duty: it shuffles the letters and is also part of the definition, so the clue reads as a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a standard bodyweight exercise, pushing yourself off the floor with your arms, done in any gym.

clue.text: Man City's manager for a season

parts.note: Pep Guardiola manages Manchester City football club
per means for each, or for a, as in 'ten pounds per head'

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of Manchester City for just one season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a noun about a football year; it is the verb meaning to add flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper food is to flavour it with ground spice, which is what seasoning a dish means.

clue.text: Destroyed recording of Taylor Swift tour before journalist

parts.note: Taylor Swift's 2023-24 world tour was called the Eras Tour
ED, short for editor, is the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone has wiped out the film of a Taylor Swift concert ahead of a journalist seeing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition, a recording that was destroyed, takes two words; the wordplay starts at 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An erased tape or file is a recording that has been wiped out, so its contents are gone for good.

clue.text: Extremely poor rent boys OK to work

indicators.note: putting materials to work turns them into something new, so these letters get reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Penniless young male prostitutes are given the go-ahead to ply their trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor rent' suggests low rent payments, but 'Extremely poor' is the definition and 'rent' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-broke is informal British slang for having no money whatsoever, utterly destitute.

clue.text: Fiery love under pressure still

indicators.note: in a down answer, being under something means coming below it, so this pair is placed second

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
fiery means burning hot
love is a zero score in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A passionate romance survives even when the couple are under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'under pressure' puts the fiery love beneath P. 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the noun for a single frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one taken from a film, so it is a photo.

clue.text: Knife cut revolutionary Australian natives

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the preceding letters are written backwards

parts.note: to knife someone is to stab them
to cut grass is to mow it

explanation.surface: A radical stabbed some indigenous Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like an adjective for the knifing; it reverses both verbs together.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombats are burrowing marsupials found only in Australia, so they are animals native to that country.

clue.text: Draw these around 9 pm in Britain

indicators.note: turned around and about, these letters are moved into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sketch these things at about nine o'clock at night in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like one cryptic definition, but the first two words are the fodder. British television has a 9 pm cut-off before which content unsuitable for children is not aired.
explanation.definitionFit: In UK broadcasting the term names the fixed evening time separating family viewing from adult programmes.

clue.text: Drink with your setter, regularly bawdy

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as ME

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: The setter invites you for a drink that turns into a bit of a raucous session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your setter' is the crossword compiler speaking of themself, a common route to ME or I.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic beverage made by fermenting honey with water, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Distance an elite athlete's beginning to run

indicators.note: running colours bleed and mix, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A top sprinter's starting run covers a certain distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distance' reads as a noun measuring the run; here it is a verb meaning to push someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to make them feel estranged, putting emotional distance between you and them.

clue.text: On reflection, awards critically examine formal beauty

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Emmys are American television awards
to try a case is to examine it judicially

explanation.surface: After some thought, the judges of prizes scrutinise classical beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like 'after thinking it over', but signals a mirror image; it turns only the awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry, balanced proportion between matching parts, is the classical notion of formal elegance in art and design.

clue.text: Line taken by glib old philosopher

indicators.note: whatever is taken by something ends up held inside it

parts.note: a pat answer is glib, too slick to be convincing
L is the standard abbreviation for line
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker adopted a slick party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old philosopher' looks like a single definition, but 'old' gives the final O and 'philosopher' alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Athenian thinker, pupil of Socrates and author of the Republic.

clue.text: Millions avoiding nearly all bigotry and exclusion

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep clear of it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
most means almost all
racism is a form of bigotry

explanation.surface: Vast numbers of people stay clear of nearly every form of prejudice and shutting others out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' tempts you to drop the last letter of 'bigotry'; instead it is MOST, which loses its M.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracism means being shut out from a group or society, deliberately shunned and excluded by others.

clue.text: Maybe order new digital filing tool

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so these letters take a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps you should order a new electronic document-filing system for the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital filing tool' sounds like office software; digits are fingers, and the filing is of nails.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board is a strip coated with abrasive grit used to file fingernails, and fingers are digits.

clue.text: Once called phone company after noon

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the first piece written is placed second

parts.note: N is short for noon
EE is a British mobile network operator

explanation.surface: A mobile network rang someone back in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the phone company behind N. EE is one of the UK's main mobile phone networks.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a maiden name, the French-derived word means born as, indicating the surname someone formerly had.

clue.text: Particular prison yard inspires film after agent turns

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one part is drawn inside another
something that turns faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent
nick is British slang for prison
E.T. is the Spielberg film
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A specific jail exercise yard inspires a movie once a spy has defected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' looks like an adjective for the prison yard; it means fussy. Nick is everyday British slang for a jail or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone particular is fussy and hard to please, insisting on precise details, which is what pernickety describes.

clue.text: Protection for the amorous Parisian landlord

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old British slang for a condom
second meaning, read literally: a French person who lets property

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a letter is one who lets, so a Parisian landlord is a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is dated British slang for a contraceptive sheath, and literally a landlord from France who lets rooms.

clue.text: Feeling sick, foolishly ate sundae

indicators.note: done foolishly means done without sense, so these letters end up in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after unwisely gobbling an ice-cream sundae.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete little story: sickness caused by overindulgence, with the fodder sitting in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nauseated means having an urge to vomit, a queasy stomach, which is exactly feeling sick.

clue.text: More senseless killing initially covered up by navy men

indicators.note: with its start hidden from view, the opening letter is lost

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors
murder is unlawful killing

explanation.surface: A pointless murder was hushed up by naval personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cover-up; 'initially covered up' just hides the first letter of the killing, which comes after the sailors in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd means ridiculous or lacking sense, so its comparative form describes something even more irrational.

clue.text: Barrel Jacob's wife lifted filled with unknown fruit

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer

indicators.note: a vessel filled with something holds it inside

parts.note: Leah was Jacob's first wife in Genesis
x, y and z are the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A barrel belonging to the biblical Jacob's wife is hoisted up, packed with some mysterious fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The unknown goes inside Leah, then the barrel and the filled wife are read upwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazelnut is the edible nut of the hazel tree; botanically a nut is a kind of dry fruit.

clue.text: British and Dutch politicians going back inside without a bloody sausage

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British

indicators.note: whatever is inside sits within the next word's letters

parts.note: lacking means without

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Politicians from Britain and the Netherlands retreat indoors, skipping a dreadful sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' reads as a British swear word; it is literal, as the sausage is made with blood. The reversed group sits inside the word for without.
explanation.definitionFit: Black pudding is a British blood sausage made from pork blood, fat and oatmeal, often served at breakfast.

clue.text: Upset team working for inventor

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down answer the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An unhappy staff is employed by a famous creator of gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset team' sounds like a disgruntled group of employees; 'Upset' turns the side over.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who devised the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: Some woozy, deconstructed music

indicators.note: taking some of a phrase means only part of it, so the letters sit within it

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A dizzy, fragmented piece of music, perhaps experimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deconstructed' hints that letters are being broken up, but the answer runs straight across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Zydeco is an accordion-led genre of dance tunes from the Creole communities of Louisiana.

clue.text: Employ American English

parts.note: US abbreviates the United States
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.walkthrough: 'Employ American English' sounds like an instruction about spelling; 'Employ' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to put it to work, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Clearly I choose the best record to spin before date with disheartened lady

indicators.note: a spinning object turns round, so the preceding letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to cull is to pick out the best from a group
an EP is an extended-play record
D is the abbreviation for date

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the outside edges of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A DJ picks out the top track to play before meeting a heartbroken woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record to spin' sounds like a DJ at work, but the spin turns back the whole run of letters from I to the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid means transparent or easily understood, so the adverb means in a lucid, transparent manner.

clue.text: True, that's funny about my grandma at the very end

indicators.note: something placed about another goes all round it

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is text-speak for finding something funny

indicators.note: the very end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a story about their grandmother right at the end of her life, insisting it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the very end' takes the last letter of both 'my' and 'grandma', and the text-speak laugh wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A true friend is a faithful one, steadfast in allegiance, which is what loyal describes.

clue.text: Headless fish in stream

indicators.note: without a head means the top is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: brill is a flatfish related to turbot

explanation.surface: A decapitated fish lies in a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface places the fish in the water; 'in' is just the link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a small brook or narrow rivulet of running water, a poetic word for a little stream.

clue.text: Mouthy art student is trying, to an extent

indicators.note: only to an extent means partly, so just a portion of the phrase is used

parts.note: runs from inside the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A cheeky art student is somewhat annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthy' means cheeky in the surface, but in the definition it means concerned with mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentistry is the skilled practice of treating teeth and gums, an art practised entirely inside patients' mouths.

clue.text: Follow the Railwaymen, finally safe after losing run

indicators.note: once something is lost it is gone, so that letter is dropped
finally points to the end, so only the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word
sure can mean safe, as in 'a sure bet'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fans follow the Railwaymen, a team finally out of relegation danger despite losing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Railwaymen' looks like a club nickname to be solved; only its last letter is used, along with that of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards as a result, coming next in sequence.

clue.text: Worried Prime Minister briefly visits retired doctor

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one part enters another
to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: cutting something brief shortens it, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: An anxious PM pops in briefly to see a GP who has stopped practising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired doctor' seems a single figure; 'retired' reverses DR, and the shortened Attlee goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rattled means nervous and unsettled, shaken up, which is what worried describes.

clue.text: Attack Tony Blair, taking sides in conflict

indicators.note: taking away a word's sides strips both its outer letters
things in conflict are at odds and in disarray, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
the surname without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Critics savage the former British Prime Minister for siding with one party in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking sides in conflict' evokes the Iraq War; it splits into an instruction to trim Blair and another to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone is an idiom meaning to assault them physically or criticise them fiercely.
